en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Ninth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether Form Has an Object:
Is form possessed of an object? Yes.
Is there for him turning toward, mental engagement, attention, volition, aspiration, and resolve?
You should not say so... [etc. ...
Is it not the case that for him there is no turning toward, mental engagement... [etc. ... nor resolve?
“Yes,” you say.
But if there is for it no turning toward, no mental application, and so forth, up to no aspiration, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
“Material form has an object.”
Contact has an object; does it have turning toward, mental advertence, and so forth, up to aspiration?
Yes. Does material form have an object; does it have turning toward, mental advertence, and so forth, up to aspiration? No.
It should not be stated thus ... [as before] ... Feeling ... perception ...

volition ... consciousness ... faith ... energy ... mindfulness ... concentration ... wisdom ... lust ... hatred ... delusion ... conceit ... wrong view ... doubt ... sloth ... restlessness ... moral shamelessness ... [and so on].
Is lack of moral dread (anottappa) accompanied by an object, and does it possess turning toward, mental advertence, ... [and so on] ...
aspiration? Yes.
Is material form (rūpa) accompanied by an object, and does it possess turning toward, mental advertence, ... [and so on] ... aspiration? [No.]
It should not be said thus ... [as before] ...
Is material form possessed of an object, yet it has no turning toward it, no mental advertence ... [as before] ...
no aspiration? Yes.
“Contact has an object; it has no turning toward, no mental advertence, ... [and so on] ... no aspiration”?
One should not say this... [and so on]. “Material form has an object; it has no turning toward, no mental advertence, ... [and so on] ... no aspiration”? [One should not say this either.]
“Yes.
“Feeling … [and so on] … non-shame has an object; it does not have turning toward, mental advertence … [and so on] … aspiration?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “form has an object”?
“Yes.
“Is it not the case that material form has a condition?
“Yes.”
If form has a condition, then indeed, O friend, you must say:
"Form has an object. The discussion on whether form has an object is finished.
